A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ADAPT research work and contain 24 readable pages, including Appendices A–B. Full-text comparison and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices without material gaps.

before.justification: v3.pdf reports original ADAPT benchmark results, efficiency measurements, and ablations in Section 4, with additional empirical analyses and experiments in Appendices A.4 and B.

after.justification: v6.pdf retains the original benchmark, efficiency, ablation, and supplementary experimental results in Section 4 and Appendices A.4 and B.

M1.justification: The Gaussian classifier, knowledge-bank construction, regularization objectives, and online/transductive procedures remain unchanged. Removing the prediction symbol from the sentence preceding Equation (2) does not change that equation or the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ImageNet distribution-shift benchmarks, ImageNet-C corruptions, ten fine-grained datasets, and appendix few-shot scenarios. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding main-text and appendix experiments. TCA remains evaluated in Tables 2 and 4; the publication-metadata update to its reference [52] does not introduce a different baseline.

E3.justification: Both retain online batch size 1, full-test-set transductive evaluation, the same backbones and accuracy metrics, alpha 0.9, and knowledge-bank sizes 16/6. The appendix evaluation settings also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component, hyperparameter, initialization, iterative-optimization, and input-order analyses are retained unchanged. Appendix tests of Gaussianity, shared covariance, corruption severity, and scarce high-confidence samples also contain the same evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 retains 100 repetitions of random feature projections and the same Henze–Zirkler and Shapiro–Wilk p-value reporting in Table 10. No run-count, seed, or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical result entries and plotted findings are unchanged, including the appendices. For example, Table 2 retains ADAPT's average accuracy of 66.53% online and 67.09% transductive under the same settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Gaussian/shared-covariance assumptions, objectives, and derivations in Section 3 and Appendix A remain unchanged. The small prose edit before Equation (2) leaves its mathematical definition intact.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about distribution-aware, source-free, backpropagation-free adaptation, closed-form inference, support for both settings, and empirical robustness and efficiency.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the Gaussian model's difficulty with complex distributions, the rationale for shared covariance, and potential adaptation delays when reliable samples accumulate slowly.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility disclosures remain unchanged, including the NVIDIA RTX A6000 hardware, hyperparameters, prototype initialization, resource measurements, and project link.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Reference [52], 'Is less more? exploring token condensation as training-free adaptation for clip,' changes from an arXiv 2024 entry to ICCV 2025, identifying the same work.

P1.justification: v6 removes the prediction symbol from one sentence in Section 3.1, replaces the first funding acknowledgment from an NRF grant to an IITP grant, updates reference [52]'s publication metadata, and changes the arXiv version/date stamp. The narrative and section structure otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer acknowledgment shifts the reference layout across pages 10–13, moving entries [16], [36], and [56] to subsequent pages. Figures 1–6, Tables 1–17, and all appendix pages remain visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: v6 makes administrative and small editorial updates, while retaining the same method, proofs, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations. The acknowledgment revision, publication-metadata update, and minor reference reflow do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
